Cooler core PCE (3.0% y/y) is a genuine medium-term positive if the disinflation trend persists and eventually shifts Fed expectations
Friday's NFP (forecast 90K vs 162K) is the week's key swing catalyst for the broad bond-market direction
Diversified composition makes BND less volatile than single-duration bets like TLT, but the directional read stays negative given current yield trajectory

calls.name: MP Materials
drivers: MP surged +4.09% to $47.29 on 9/30, its third straight day of high volatility, on strong Q2 operating momentum: revenue +89% YoY, NdPr production +41%, and adjusted EBITDA turning positive
New long-term gadolinium offtake agreement with a major US aerospace/defense customer, plus a new Texas 10X magnet facility in Northlake, extends MP's mine-to-magnet integration
Existing $400M DoD preferred-equity stake (~15% ownership), $110/kg NdPr price floor, and $150M separation-capacity loan continue to underpin the government-backed re-rating thesis
China's rare-earth export controls remain suspended only until 10 Nov 2026 -- a live re-escalation catalyst that could re-accelerate the ex-China re-rating trade if China re-imposes curbs

calls.name: Lynas Rare Earths
drivers: LYC.AX rose +1.39% to A$13.83 on 9/30 after Lynas confirmed it entered takeover discussions during 2026, though the negotiations reportedly collapsed with the suitor still unidentified -- speculative M&A interest remains a live catalyst
Gina Rinehart's rare-earth stakes (MP + Lynas) have lost an estimated A$680M (~$478M) in value over the past year, reflecting the sector's volatility even as the structural ex-China thesis holds
China's rare-earth export-control suspension expires 10 Nov 2026 -- a binary near-term catalyst that could re-rate the entire ex-China basket if curbs return
Lynas remains the largest ex-China rare-earth separator, giving it direct exposure to Western government efforts to build parallel supply chains

calls.name: Energy Fuels
drivers: UUUU rose a modest +0.36% to $11.03 on 9/30, a much calmer move than MP/Lynas, consistent with the broader rare-earth-miner complex stabilizing after recent volatility
Energy Fuels remains one of the few US-based rare-earth/uranium dual-exposure names, giving it a secondary read-through on the uranium/power-demand theme (see URA call) alongside rare earths
China's rare-earth export-control suspension expiring 10 Nov 2026 is the same live re-escalation catalyst relevant across the ex-China basket
No fresh company-specific catalyst (offtake, DoD contract) identified for Energy Fuels this run, keeping conviction moderate versus MP/USAR

calls.name: USA Rare Earth
drivers: USA Rare Earth secured a $1.6B government funding commitment in Sept 2026 (Commerce Dept/Cantor Fitzgerald involvement), including a $1.3B loan and $277M in funding for a 16.1% government equity stake
The Department of War committed $750M to a Special Purpose Vehicle for the Serra Verde offtake plus a forward-purchase contract for at least $300M of rare-earth products over five years
This level of direct US government backing mirrors the MP Materials DoD-partnership playbook and materially de-risks USAR's balance sheet and offtake economics
China's rare-earth export-control suspension expiring 10 Nov 2026 remains a live sector-wide re-escalation catalyst that would likely benefit USAR alongside MP/Lynas

calls.name: VanEck Rare Earth/Strategic Metals ETF
drivers: REMX is a basket proxy for the ex-China rare-earth re-rating theme, tracking constituents like MP (+4.09% 9/30) and Lynas (+1.39% 9/30) directly
China's rare-earth export-control suspension expiring 10 Nov 2026 is the dominant sector-wide catalyst -- a live re-escalation risk that would likely re-accelerate the entire ex-China basket
Heavy US government backing across the sector (MP's $400M DoD stake, USAR's $1.6B funding commitment) provides a structural floor under the ex-China supply-chain buildout thesis
Basket-level diversification smooths some single-name volatility (e.g., MP's sharper swings vs UUUU's calmer moves) but doesn't eliminate the shared China-export-control binary risk

callsNote: Updated Wed 30 Sep 2026 (~07:02am SGT). Latest completed US cash session = Tue 29 Sep close, a much calmer, more orderly session than Monday's forced-deleveraging shock: S&P -0.17% to 7,670.84, Nasdaq -0.09%, Dow -0.26%, Russell -0.35%, and VIX itself eased -0.19% to 16.04. Gold and silver rebounded back into their traditional hedge role (GLD +1.32%, SLV +0.96%, GDX +1.34%) as bargain buyers returned ahead of China's Golden Week -- the opposite of Monday's crash-together dynamic. Oil eased modestly for a real reason: Middle East crude exports are rebounding toward pre-war levels as Saudi Arabia's repaired East-West pipeline resumed flow, easing the Hormuz risk premium. CORRECTION mid-run: the price spine's raw Brent/WTI front-month futures bars for 9/29 (-8.65%/-3.61%) turned out to be contract-roll data artifacts (volume collapsed to a few hundred/few thousand contracts vs tens of thousands the prior session); cross-checked wire reports (CNBC/Reuters) put the real Brent move at roughly -2.6% to ~$102.59, a modest pullback rather than a dramatic energy crash. USO's own -4.44% ETF print is a real traded price but notably sharper than that corrected benchmark move, so its EV/pUp were only lightly trimmed rather than cut hard; XLE (-0.90%, a real modest move) was trimmed lightly too. Material revisions this run: GLD and SLV both upgraded back toward the top of their recent range on the confirmed hedge-role rebound. The rare-earth basket (MP -2.20%, LYC.AX -0.94%, UUUU -0.36%) was revised to reflect Tuesday's much milder declines versus Monday, with a new driver flagging China's Oct-2025 export-control suspension expiring 10 Nov 2026 as a live re-escalation catalyst to watch. Bonds (TLT/IEF/LQD/HYG/EMB/BND) stay under pressure given the 30Y broke above 5.6% Tue 9/29, its highest level since June 2002, even as equities calmed. Crypto calls note an incremental regulatory tailwind (SEC's new generic listing standards shortening crypto ETP approval timelines) partially offsetting the still-elevated-real-yield headwind. USD/Cash was trimmed from OW to modest OW as the acute panic-driven cash bid from Monday faded with Tuesday's calmer tape, though structurally elevated yields continue to support the dollar. This week's dominant scheduled catalysts remain US Core PCE and Final GDP (today, 30 Sep), ISM Manufacturing PMI (1 Oct), an unusually dense Fed-speaker slate continuing all week, and 2 Oct payrolls (forecast 90K vs 162K prior, unemployment forecast 4.1%).
